requirements.text: An email was received from Carlos reporting an issue with his assigned workstation ... identify the configuration item currently assigned to him ... log a new incident to document this issue, marking it with high impact and high urgency
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND caller_id = 'USER_003' AND configuration_item = 'CI_001' AND channel = 'email' AND status = 'new' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%device%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%shutdown%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023); the only incident the task creates
Carlos resolved to USER_003 (carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com, agent, active), the only Carlos on the seed; he is the affected user, so caller_id

'the configuration item currently assigned to him' is CI_001 (Carlos Laptop, owner_id USER_003, status in_use, so policy 5.1 allows the link); the only CI owned by USER_003, although the request calls it a workstation
channel = email from the request's 'An email was received from Carlos'; the benchmark's channel = phone is contradicted by the request and repaired (the seed uses email as a channel value)

priority = critical from the policy 3.1 matrix (impact high x urgency high); the benchmark's priority = high is contradicted by the policy and repaired; the seed does not decide it (its six high/high incidents split three critical, three high)
status = new by policy 3.1 (all new incidents are set to status = new); the request asks for no transition

short_description wording not fixed by the request; the benchmark's LIKE '%device%' and LIKE '%shutdown%' are kept (the request says 'The device also becomes unusually warm' and 'workstation shutdown')
service, assigned_to and assignment_group not stated and not tested; opened_by is mandatory by policy 3.1 but the incident table has no such column

requirements.text: determine the appropriate high-priority SLA and associate it with the incident so response timelines are enforced
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_sla_id = 'TSLA_011' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND sla_def_id = 'SLA_002' AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (TSLA_011 after TSLA_010); the request names one SLA, so the only incident_sla row the task creates

'the appropriate high-priority SLA' is SLA_002 (High Priority Resolution SLA, applies_to_priority high, ORG_001, Carlos's org, active), the only high-priority definition in ORG_001; SLA_008 is ORG_002's definition of the same name

the request's words fix the high-priority SLA even though the incident's policy priority is critical; policy 6 (SLAs aligned on priority) would point to SLA_001 (Critical Response SLA, ORG_001), but the request does not leave the SLA open, so the tension is recorded here
stage = in_progress kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the seed's active SLA rows use in_progress)
has_breached and start_time are mandatory columns the request does not fix; not tested

requirements.text: notify the user that the issue has been logged for workstation shutdown and is under investigation
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND email = 'carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com' AND type = 'alert' AND status = 'queued' AND LOWER(subject) LIKE '%incident%' AND LOWER(subject) LIKE '%workstation%' AND LOWER(subject) LIKE '%shutdown%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%issue%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%carlos%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%logged%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%currently%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%investigation%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%problem%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the only notification the task creates
'the user' is Carlos, USER_003, whose seed email is carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com; the notification references the incident this task creates, INC_024
type = alert and status = queued kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the seed uses both values)
subject keywords incident, workstation, shutdown kept from the benchmark check; the request fixes no subject
message keywords issue, logged and investigation are the request's own words; carlos, currently and problem are kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
the benchmark's LOWER(subject) LIKE '%Incident%' patterns are lowercased here; SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII, so the meaning is unchanged

disagreement: disposition: A kept the benchmark's message terms carlos, currently and problem, B dropped them (repaired) because a message in the request's words contains none; chose A because the request gives the message's gist in indirect speech, not its wording, so a message that names Carlos or says the problem is currently under investigation is not contradicted, and the benchmark's check is the prior

requirements.text: determine the appropriate high-priority SLA and associate it with the incident (one SLA, not the ORG_002 copy or the critical one)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND sla_def_id <> 'SLA_002'
assumptions: boundary of the SLA selector: SLA_008 (High Priority Resolution SLA, ORG_002) shares SLA_002's name and priority, and SLA_001 (Critical Response SLA) matches the matrix priority; the request asks for one SLA, so no other definition may be linked to INC_024

disagreement: A has this stay, B does not; kept because the anchored TSLA_011 requirement cannot catch a second SLA row linked to INC_024, and two near-matching definitions make this a real selector boundary

Verify Incident CI.evidence: two cells: channel = phone is contradicted by the request's first words 'An email was received from Carlos' (the seed's channel values include email), so channel = email; priority = high is contradicted by policy 3.1's matrix, where impact high and urgency high give critical, so priority = critical. The other cells (CI_001, USER_003, status new, impact and urgency high, the short_description keywords) are kept. The seed is mixed on high x high (three incidents critical, three high) and does not decide it.

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the incident INC_024 (caller USER_003, CI_001, channel repaired to email, status new, high/high, priority repaired to critical, short_description LIKE device and shutdown) and the SLA link TSLA_011 (SLA_002, in_progress), with 'Verify Incident CI' repaired identically by both and 'Verify Incident Link to SLA' kept by both.
disagreement: disposition of 'Verify notification': A kept (all the benchmark's subject and message terms), B repaired (dropped the message terms carlos, currently and problem as absent from a message in the request's words); chose A's kept form because the request gives the message's gist in indirect speech and fixes no wording, so those terms are not contradicted and the benchmark's check is the prior (logged on the requirement); they remain the likeliest false-failure source.
disagreement: stay that no incident_sla row other than SLA_002 is linked to INC_024 (expected 0): A has it, B does not; kept as the boundary of the SLA selector, since SLA_008 shares SLA_002's name and SLA_001 matches the matrix priority, and the anchored TSLA_011 requirement cannot catch a second linked row (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: stay that the count of incidents on CI_003 (Kenji Workstation, the only CI named workstation) stays at its seed value 4: B has it, A does not; dropped because the incident requirement's anchored cell configuration_item = CI_001 already fails an incident logged against CI_003, so the stay would only catch a second incident, a collateral change measured separately rather than a selector boundary.
The benchmark's priority high and its choice of the high-priority SLA look like one reading (high x high = high); the policy's matrix says critical, so the incident priority is repaired to critical while the SLA stays SLA_002 because the request names the high-priority SLA in words; a reviewer who prefers the policy's alignment over the request's words should change sla_def_id to SLA_001. If the scorer's tool computes priority as high, the incident requirement fails on that cell alone. Policy 7 (search knowledge on incident creation) gives no requirement: none of KB_001 to KB_005 (password reset, Outlook configuration, desktop boot, locked email accounts, email access) covers unexpected shutdowns or overheating, and no listed tool searches or links knowledge. 'Verify Carlos user details' is read-only and leaves no state.
revised: the stay on other SLA links to INC_024 no longer repeats incident_id and sla_def_id in its cells, since its selector already fixes both; the sql and count are unchanged.
